title: POC Weekly Sync — model safety net and pin pruning
summary: Weekly POC sync focused on pruning pinned model versions, agreeing on a safety-net fallback catalog, and defining emergency unpin/rollback runbook. Team agreed to run two short A/B runs to validate quantized variant under 250ms p50 and to share updated model catalog and audit examples. Action items assigned for pricing impact, security docs, and a tabletop failover drill next week.
action_items: Maya Chen - share updated model catalog CSV with quantization/latency columns - 2027-01-14
Diego Alvarez - run 2 A/B runs (unquantized vs 8-bit quantized) on resident dataset and produce latency/cost chart - 2027-01-13
Tom Reynolds - provide safety prompt set (50 queries) for quality regression checks - 2027-01-12
Evan Brooks - confirm KMS key rotation constraints and provide sample audit log snippet - 2027-01-15
Priya Nishtar - schedule tabletop failover drill and invite RSM + SRE - 2027-01-17
next_steps: Redwood to send updated catalog and fallback mapping
Customer to run A/B and return results
Schedule failover tabletop for next Tuesday
Redwood to attach SOC2 + KMS integration notes to the deck
transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-01-10 11:00 PST — Duration approx 45 min. Attendees listed above.

[00:00] Maya Chen: Okay, thanks everyone for joining, uh, today is the weekly POC sync — we're focusing on the pin pruning proposal and the safety net fallback mapping. Quick roll call?
[00:08] Tom Reynolds: Tom here.
[00:10] Lisa Park: Lisa.
[00:11] Diego Alvarez: Diego from Redwood.
[00:13] Evan Brooks: Evan, security.
[00:15] Priya Nishtar: Priya, CSM.
[00:17] Nora Patel: Nora.
[00:19] Raj Malhotra: Raj, SRE.
[00:21] Maya Chen: Great. High level: last week we pinned two model families for the POC — the baseline L-Replica-2 and the quantized Q-lite variant. We heard concerns about running too many pinned versions which increases catalog surface and complicates rollbacks. Today's goal: agree on a pruning strategy and explicit fallback rules so engineering has an unambiguous runbook.

[00:45] Lisa Park: Yeah, from our side we've been seeing catalog drift in staging, and it's getting noisy in the routing layer. If we keep old pins around for months we end up with stale latencies and some teams hit the wrong variant.
[01:02] Tom Reynolds: Exactly. We want a pragmatic approach: keep a short runway for pins, prefer soft-fallbacks first, but have emergency unpin steps documented.

[01:28] Diego Alvarez: Quick clarification — when you say "short runway" are you thinking 1 week, 2 weeks? We have customers doing 72 hours, others go 14 days. There's a design tradeoff: shorter runway reduces complexity but may not catch intermittent regressions.
[01:48] Tom Reynolds: I think 7 days is reasonable for us for model experiments; for production-like anchors maybe 14. But we need a safety-net catalog of smaller, compatible models that can act as automatic fallbacks.

[02:10] Maya Chen: So proposal: prune pins older than 14 days unless flagged as "prod-stable". Maintain a fallback catalog with 3 tiers: primary pinned model, warm fallback (same family quantized), and cold fallback (smaller architecture). The routing policy will attempt primary -> warm -> cold, and finally region-level reroute.

[02:40] Nora Patel: That sounds good. Two questions — what's the expected latency delta with the warm fallback (quantized)? And how do we measure quality delta?

[02:53] Diego Alvarez: From our internal, quantized 8-bit usually reduces cost by ~40% and adds 10-20ms p50 on T4-ish hardware, sometimes more at long sequences. But key is running your prompt set. We recommended a 50-query safety prompt set to measure semantic regression; Tom, can you provide that?

[03:17] Tom Reynolds: Yes, I'll pull together 50 representative queries by tomorrow.

[03:22] Evan Brooks: On the security side, the fallback path needs to preserve same encryption and audit log semantics. We can't have a fallback that bypasses key access policies or emits different retention tags.
[03:36] Maya Chen: Absolutely. Our Private deployments keep KMS the same; for hosted we can map to customer-managed keys (CMK) and ensure audit logs record route and model used. We'll attach an example audit entry.

[03:54] Evan Brooks: Also, if fallback triggers blackbox unplanned, we need notification escalation — an event to SRE and to our legal/compliance inbox if data residency changes.

[04:08] Raj Malhotra: For SRE, we need clear circuit-breaker thresholds e.g., 5xx rate > 0.5% or p95 latency > 1.2x baseline for 2 continuous minutes triggers failover to warm fallback. Can we codify those?

[04:26] Diego Alvarez: Yes, we can attach a suggested circuit-breaker JSON. It'll include p50/p95 thresholds and error rate triggers. We can also expose a manual unpin API for emergencies.

[04:41] Lisa Park: Manual unpin API is critical. We had an incident where a model degraded quietly and auto-routing kept serving it. Need an immediate kill switch.

[04:50] Maya Chen: Noted — manual unpin plus automated rollback policy. Diego, can you outline emergency unpin steps?

[05:02] Diego Alvarez: Sure: (1) Toggle model flag to drain new sessions. (2) Route inflight to warm fallback via weight shift for 30s. (3) If errors persist, perform model swap on gateway and push toggle in config store, (4) run a health check and if green mark new model as active. We'll document exact API calls.

[05:25] Tom Reynolds: Will that preserve KV cache compatibility across variants? We rely on prefix caching for long conversations.

[05:33] Diego Alvarez: Good catch. Cache compatibility depends on model architecture; between same family quantized variants KV cache is compatible, but swapping to a different architecture will flush cache. We'll mark that in the runbook — that's a quality hit.

[05:48] Maya Chen: Let's call that a "stateful swap" penalty. We can enumerate which fallbacks preserve KV cache in the catalog CSV.

[06:01] Lisa Park: About pin pruning — can we automate TTL-based pruning and also require a custodian tag before final deletion? So someone must approve before removal of a pin from history.

[06:13] Diego Alvarez: Yes, add a two-step lifecycle: prune -> archive -> delete. Archive keeps the version in storage for 30 days and a custodian must approve deletion.

[06:25] Nora Patel: Sounds safe. One more — we need to understand cost impact if we default to warm fallback more often. Can you model expected monthly cost delta?

[06:35] Maya Chen: We can provide a sensitivity table: baseline cost, warm fallback cost, and cold fallback cost across your query volume. Diego, can you prepare a short cost delta slide?

[06:45] Diego Alvarez: Yup, will produce a chart.

[07:00] Tom Reynolds: For the A/B runs: we'll send two days of traffic (10k queries) and route half to unquantized and half to quantized. We want Redwood to record per-token latency and token cost breakdowns.

[07:14] Maya Chen: We'll enable per-token breakdowns and provide logs with model id tags. Expect CSV with p50/p95 and cost per 1000 tokens.

[07:22] Evan Brooks: Also we need proof that audit logs include model id and user token hash. Can't have anonymous traces.

[07:30] Diego Alvarez: We'll attach a sample audit log schema that includes model_name, model_hash, routing_decision, and key_id.

[07:42] Lisa Park: On the quality checks — what metrics do you suggest besides semantic similarity? F1? BLEU? Those don't map well.

[07:52] Diego Alvarez: For retrieval-style tasks use recall@k and for generation do embedding cosine similarity plus human review of 50 critical prompts. We'll compute mean embedding distance delta and flag > 0.08 as potential regression threshold.

[08:12] Tom Reynolds: Good. We'll run the embedding similarity and send back results.

[08:22] Maya Chen: Let's talk timeline and concrete steps this week: Tom to send safety prompts by 2027-01-12; Diego to run A/B job by 2027-01-13; Maya to send catalog and fallback mapping by 2027-01-14; Priya to schedule failover tabletop on the 17th.

[08:45] Raj Malhotra: For tabletop I'd like to include network partition scenarios and a simulated KMS key rotation; we need to ensure fail-open isn't happening.

[08:55] Evan Brooks: On KMS rotation: our compliance team requires a 30-day notice for key rotation windows. If Redwood needs to rotate keys in a private deployment we must be alerted; can't have silent rotation.

[09:07] Diego Alvarez: We respect rotation windows. We'll add a KMS interactive diagram to the security notes.

[09:20] Lisa Park: Any blockers we should surface? For us, the only blocker is getting the safety prompts and SRE availability for the tabletop.

[09:29] Maya Chen: On Redwood's side, blocker is finalize catalog mapping and provide quickstart for manual unpin API. We'll prioritize both.

[09:40] Tom Reynolds: Quick question — could Redwood support region-level fallback so if one region hits capacity the request routes to a lower-cost region but same model fingerprint? Data residency might complicate that.

[09:55] Diego Alvarez: We can route cross-region but only if your data residency policy allows. For Private deployments we can enable regional routing with same KMS. For hosted we'll need your residency flags. We'll add flags to the catalog.

[10:08] Maya Chen: Time check — about 10 minutes left. Any other items?

[10:15] Nora Patel: One small ask: include a column for "cache_compatibility" and "expected_cache_loss_seconds" in the catalog CSV. That helps us plan stateful conversation fallbacks.

[10:25] Maya Chen: Great suggestion — Diego will include that.

[10:32] Priya Nishtar: I'll take care of the calendar invite for the tabletop and attach the runbook draft.

[10:38] Maya Chen: Okay let's recap action items: Maya share catalog (14th), Diego run A/B and cost chart (13th), Tom supply prompts (12th), Evan to share KMS constraints (15th), Priya schedule tabletop (17th). We'll also add the circuit-breaker thresholds and manual unpin API docs to the shared drive.

[10:55] Lisa Park: Sounds good, thanks.
[11:00] Maya Chen: Thank you all — we'll follow up in email with links. Meeting adjourned.

Notes: Transcript has occasional transcription errors and simplified speaker labels; timestamps approximate. Shared artifacts referenced: model_catalog_20270114.csv (to be sent), circuit_breaker_suggestion.json, audit_log_example.txt, A/B_results_template.csv.
